# phonometry

> Acoustic measurement, analysis and prediction in Python. Sound level metrology, psychoacoustics, room and building acoustics, materials, vibration, environmental and transport noise, underwater acoustics, electroacoustics and wave simulation, with every metric implemented from the text of its governing standard and 1897 numerical conformance checks enforced in CI, against 230 normative designations and 121 further published sources.

phonometry v4.0.0rc1 is a pure-Python library built on NumPy/SciPy (Python >= 3.12). Each result is a typed, frozen dataclass that carries the inputs it was computed from, draws its own figure with a one-line `.plot()` in English or Spanish, and, where a standard defines a reporting format, renders that format as a PDF with `.report()`. The conformance report pins each of the 1897 checks to a standard, a clause or table, the normative expected value and the value the library computes, across 111 domains.

The project was published as **PyOctaveBand** until version 3.0.0. Third-party references and dependency pins still using that name refer to this library.

Install:

```bash
pip install phonometry              # core (NumPy + SciPy only)
pip install "phonometry[plot]"      # + matplotlib figures and .plot()
pip install "phonometry[perf]"      # + numba-jitted impulse kernel
pip install "phonometry[report]"    # + reportlab and svglib, for .report() PDF fiches
pip install "phonometry[audio]"     # + python-soundfile, for FLAC, AIFF, Ogg/Opus, MP3 and compressed WAV
pip install "phonometry[full]"      # all of the above (recommended)
pip install "phonometry[torch]"     # + torch and array-api-compat, the FDTD engines on PyTorch; not in [full]
```

I recommend `pip install "phonometry[full]"`, which enables every feature except the torch backend of the FDTD engines, which `[torch]` adds. On 32-bit Windows and 32-bit Linux, where numba, and so `[full]`, is not supported, `pip install "phonometry[plot,report,audio]"` installs the other three extras. The base install computes every metric on NumPy and SciPy alone; without the extras only the `.plot()` figures, the `.report()` PDF fiches (whose figure panel needs matplotlib as well as reportlab and svglib), the compressed audio formats and the torch backend of the FDTD engines are unavailable. The `impulse` time weighting still works without numba, on a pure-Python kernel that is only slower, and the FDTD engines run on NumPy either way, and on an NVIDIA GPU once CuPy is installed. `[full]` leaves torch out because the torch wheels PyPI serves on Linux bring gigabytes of CUDA libraries; on a Linux machine without an NVIDIA GPU, running `pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu` before `pip install "phonometry[torch]"` takes the CPU wheels instead.

One caveat about `[full]`: numba is the only extra that caps NumPy, and it raises that cap only once it supports a new NumPy minor, so in the weeks after a NumPy minor release `phonometry[full]` (like `phonometry[perf]`) can resolve one minor behind what a plain install gets. numba only makes the `impulse` time weighting faster, so install `phonometry[plot,report]` instead if you need the newest NumPy the day it ships.

Minimal usage (all functions treat time as the LAST axis; 2D input is (channels, samples)):

```python
import numpy as np
from phonometry import filters, signals

fs = 48000
x = np.random.randn(fs)              # 1 s of signal (pressure units)
bands = filters.octave_filter(x, fs, fraction=3)         # 1/3-octave bands
spl, freq = bands.levels, bands.frequencies
la = signals.laeq(x, fs)                                 # A-weighted Leq
stats = signals.ln_levels(x, fs, n=(10, 50, 90))         # statistical levels
```

If you are an AI assistant setting this up for a user: install from PyPI (no system dependencies on Linux with glibc on x86-64 or ARM64, on macOS on ARM or on 64-bit Windows; Getting Started says what other platforms build from source), remember integer audio (e.g. wavfile.read int16) is handled automatically, use `calibration_factor` from `sensitivity()` for real dB SPL, and prefer `OctaveFilterBank` over repeated `octave_filter()` calls in tight loops (although designs are cached either way). The library computes standardized quantities; it is not a certified instrument and does not acquire data from hardware.

## Start here

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/): Where to begin with phonometry: the first analysis end to end, the task index, the map of all the guides, why the library exists and who maintains it.
- [What do you need to measure?](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/tasks/): The task-shaped door into the guides: a job on the left, the guide that answers it on the right, with the standard it implements.
- [Getting Started](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/getting-started/): Install phonometry, run your first one-third-octave analysis and calibrate it.
- [Environments](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/environments/): Where phonometry runs and how to install it there: pip and uv, conda, Jupyter, JupyterLite, Docker and type checkers, with what each one supports.
- [pip and uv](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/environments/pip-and-uv/): Install phonometry with pip or uv on Python 3.12 to 3.14: each extra and what it brings, torch without CUDA, a uv project and an install from a clone.
- [conda and mamba](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/environments/conda/): Use phonometry in a conda or mamba environment: its dependencies from conda-forge under their names there, then phonometry itself with pip.
- [Jupyter and JupyterLab](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/environments/jupyter/): Use phonometry in Jupyter and JupyterLab: the kernel and the extras, record tables, inline and SVG figures, videos, fiches and warnings in a cell.
- [JupyterLite and Pyodide](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/environments/jupyterlite/): phonometry in a browser through JupyterLite or Pyodide: the extras micropip can install, what runs there, what cannot, and a JupyterLite site of your own.
- [Docker and servers](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/environments/docker/): Run phonometry in a container or on a server: a slim image with a virtual environment, any user id, a read-only root and ffmpeg for videos.
- [Type checking](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/environments/type-checking/): Type-check code that uses phonometry with mypy or pyright: the wheel ships py.typed, choices and numbers are checked, and the FDTD fields are typed Any.
- [Why phonometry](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/why-phonometry/): Conformance first: an IEC 61672-1 time-weighting case study, the conformance suite, defects in the standards, and phonometry's place in Python.
- [Upgrading from 3.3 to 4.0](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/upgrading/): Upgrade to 4.0: what moved, was renamed or removed and how to find its new spelling, the root trim, split modules and units in parameter names.
- [About](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/about/): About phonometry: who maintains it, how each metric is built from its governing standard and checked in CI, how to report an error and how to cite it.
- [Support the project](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/support/): Support for phonometry: reporting numbers that look wrong, sponsoring the work and helping obtain primary sources that no legitimate route has yielded.
- [Guides index](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/guides/): All 168 guides of phonometry in the thirteen topics it covers: what each area is for, the standards it implements and a one-line summary of every guide.
- [Glossary of quantities](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/glossary/): Acoustic quantities the guides compute most, each with symbol, one-sentence definition, unit, defining standard and clause, and the guide computing it.

## Signal analysis

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/): Measurement core: octave filter banks, frequency and time weighting, levels, calibrated spectra, calibration, uncertainty and a sound level meter in code.
- [Build a sound level meter](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/sound-level-meter/): Sound level meter built from the API: IEC 60942 calibration, IEC 61672-1 weightings, Leq, SEL, percentiles, IEC 61260-1 bands and class checks.

### Octave filtering

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/filters/): Fractional octave analysis: ANSI S1.11 / IEC 61260-1 filter banks, architectures, class verification, block processing and multichannel analysis. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-signals-filters.txt)
- [Octave and Fractional-Octave Filter Banks](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/filters/filter-banks/): Octave and fractional-octave band levels in Python: band mathematics, the octave_filter parameters, the parametric EQ, band signals and zero-phase filtering.
- [Filter Architecture Gallery](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/filters/filter-gallery/): Five band-filter architectures compared at the band edges, their 1/1 and 1/3 octave responses, usage examples and the Linkwitz-Riley crossover.
- [Filter class verification (IEC 61260-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/filters/filter-compliance/): Filter class by IEC 61260-1:2014: the Table 1 mask, IEC 61260-2 bandwidth and summation, class 0 (1995) and IEC 61260-3 periodic tests.
- [Block Processing](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/filters/block-processing/): Streaming with carried filter state: blocks bit-identical to one pass, per-channel state, the pitfalls and a real-time level meter.
- [Multichannel and Performance](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/filters/multichannel/): Per-channel processing of multichannel recordings: the (channels, samples) convention, calibrating an array capsule by capsule, and where the time goes.

### Levels and weighting

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/levels/): IEC 61672-1 and special weightings, Fast/Slow/Impulse, integrated, statistical and dose levels, and the ISO 1996 indicators built on them. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-signals-levels.txt)
- [Frequency Weighting (A, C, Z)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/levels/weighting/): A/C/Z frequency weighting by IEC 61672-1, class 1 with a high-frequency accuracy mode, verified against the Table 3 tolerances.
- [Special Weightings (G, B, D, AU)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/levels/special-weightings/): G-weighting for infrasound (ISO 7196), historical B (ANSI S1.4-1983) and D (IEC 537), AU (IEC 61012) in the presence of ultrasound, and B and AU checks.
- [Time Weighting and Integration](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/levels/time-weighting/): IEC 61672-1:2013 exponential detector: Fast and Slow, the dropped Impulse ballistics, tone-burst verification (Table 4), initial state and streaming.
- [Integrated and Statistical Levels](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/levels/levels/): Leq, LAeq, L10/L50/L90 percentile levels, LCpeak/SEL and noise dose (IEC 61252), and octave spectrograms, with the ISO 1996 indicators in their own guide.

### Signals and spectra

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/spectra/): Frequency- and time-domain analysis: calibrated Welch spectra and their quality, cepstrum and echoes, the envelope spectrum, correlation and time delay. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-signals-spectra.txt)
- [Calibrated spectral analysis (Bendat & Piersol)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/spectra/spectral-analysis/): Welch spectra (Bendat & Piersol) with random errors, confidence intervals, coherent output, smoothing, colored noise and multitaper.
- [Multiple and partial coherence (Bendat & Piersol)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/spectra/miso-coherence/): Ordinary, multiple and partial coherence of correlated sources driving one response (Bendat & Piersol), to find which source dominates each band.
- [Time-frequency analysis](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/spectra/time-frequency/): Calibrated STFT spectrogram in dB SPL, the time-frequency trade-off, and the Bendat & Piersol zoom FFT for tones closer than a bin.
- [Cepstrum, echoes and the envelope spectrum (Havelock / Bendat & Piersol)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/spectra/cepstrum-echoes/): Power, real and complex cepstrum: echoes and their reflection coefficient, liftering, the homomorphic round trip and the envelope spectrum.
- [Time synchronous averaging (McFadden 1987)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/spectra/synchronous-averaging/): Synchronous averaging of a periodic waveform in asynchronous noise (McFadden 1987): the comb filter, the square-root law and non-integer periods.
- [Correlation, time delay and envelope (Bendat & Piersol / Knapp & Carter)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/spectra/correlation-delay/): Bendat & Piersol correlation, time delay by correlator, phase slope or Knapp & Carter GCC, sub-sample alignment and the Hilbert envelope.
- [Test signals and sample-rate tools (IEC 60268-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/spectra/test-signals/): IEC 60268-1 tone bursts with exact gating, colored noise, polyphase resampling with explicit anti-alias, and fractional delay.
- [System measurement: Golay, shaped sweeps, inversion](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/spectra/system-measurement/): Impulse responses from Golay pairs with exactly noise-free deconvolution, sweeps shaped to a target spectrum, and Kirkeby-regularized inversion.

### Calibration and uncertainty

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/): Defensible measurement: SPL calibration versus dBFS, GUM and Monte Carlo uncertainty, record qualification and class verifiers. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-signals-metrology.txt)
- [Calibration and dBFS](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/calibration/): Sensitivity factor from digital units to pascals: an IEC 60942 calibrator or a rated microphone sensitivity, the calibrator's own verdict, and dBFS.
- [Measurement uncertainty (GUM and Monte Carlo)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/gum-uncertainty/): GUM law of propagation (ISO/IEC Guide 98-3:2008) and Monte Carlo (Supplement 1): combined and expanded uncertainty, Type B, coverage intervals.
- [Compliance and verification](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/compliance-verification/): Classes of IEC 61672-1 and IEC 61260-1: what they claim, design verifiers, the IEC TC 29 rule, the conformance report and what needs a laboratory.
- [Data qualification: stationarity, level crossings and peaks (Bendat & Piersol)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/data-qualification/): Qualification of a random record before analysis: Bendat & Piersol stationarity (reverse arrangements, runs) and Rice peak statistics.
- [Random-incidence and diffuse-field response (IEC 61183)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/random-incidence/): Random incidence on a sound level meter: the IEC 61183:1994 directivity factor, and the random-incidence and diffuse-field sensitivity levels.
- [Free-field corrections of a sound level meter (IEC 62585)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/free-field-corrections/): IEC 62585:2012 corrections for a sound level meter's periodic test: the adjustment value, free-field corrections, Annex I uncertainty, verdict and fiche.
- [Periodic tests of a sound level meter (IEC 61672-3)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/sound-level-meter-periodic-tests/): IEC 61672-3:2013 verdict on a working sound level meter from a laboratory's periodic tests, clause by clause against IEC 61672-1.

### Microphone calibration (IEC 61094)

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/): Defensible measurement: SPL calibration versus dBFS, GUM and Monte Carlo uncertainty, record qualification and class verifiers. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-signals-metrology-microphones.txt)
- [Microphone calibration by comparison (IEC 61094-5 and IEC 61094-8)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/comparison-calibration/): Calibration by comparison (IEC 61094-5/-8): a reference sensitivity carried to a working standard in level and phase, corrections and uncertainty.
- [Microphone calibration by reciprocity (IEC 61094-2 and IEC 61094-3)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/signals/metrology/reciprocity-calibration/): Calibration by reciprocity (IEC 61094-2/-3): laboratory standard microphones without a reference, three pair measurements, coupler or free field.

## The medium

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/fluids/): Medium of propagation computed from measured, not assumed, conditions: humid air by IEC 61094-2:2009 Annex F, and why every domain uses it.
- [Humid air](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/fluids/humid-air/): Humid air by IEC 61094-2:2009 Annex F (CIPM-2007): density, speed of sound, ratio of specific heats, viscosity and thermal diffusivity.

## Elastic solids

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/solids/): Elastic constants of a solid and the three longitudinal wave speeds they give: which one a printed table holds and how to get from one to another.
- [Wave speeds of a solid](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/solids/wave-speeds/): Beam, plate and unbounded: the three longitudinal wave speeds of a solid, which one a printed table holds, and the inverse that returns Young's modulus.

## Files

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/io/): File layer of a measurement: calibrated WAV, block streaming, BWF with bext provenance, the calibration sidecar, material catalogues and video.
- [Reading and writing measurement audio](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/io/audio-files/): Audio files as measurement records: a meter's WAV into a calibrated Signal, overnight recordings in blocks, BWF with bext and the calibration sidecar.
- [Your own catalogues](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/io/material-catalogues/): Data sheets, declarations of performance, test reports or your own measurements as JSON or CSV catalogue files that the library's models read.
- [Writing animations and FDTD runs to video](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/io/videos/): Any matplotlib animation to WebM, MP4 or GIF through ffmpeg: the encoder found by a trial encode, hardware first, and FDTD runs written straight to video.

## Hearing and perception

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/): Perception of sound and what noise does to hearing: loudness, sharpness, roughness, tonality, annoyance, STI and SII, thresholds and exposure.

### Psychoacoustics

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/psychoacoustics/): Loudness (ISO 532, ECMA-418-2), sharpness, tonality, roughness, fluctuation strength, tonal assessment (ECMA-418-1, ISO/PAS 20065) and annoyance. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-perception-psychoacoustics.txt)
- [Loudness](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/psychoacoustics/loudness/): Zwicker loudness in sones (ISO 532-1) and the ISO 226:2023 equal-loudness contours, with the ISO 532-2/-3 and ECMA-418-2 models in their own guide.
- [Advanced Loudness (ISO 532-2/-3, ECMA-418-2)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/psychoacoustics/advanced-loudness/): ERB_N and the Cam scale, Moore-Glasberg loudness (ISO 532-2), time-varying loudness (ISO 532-3), Sottek loudness (ECMA-418-2) and which model to choose.
- [Sound Quality Metrics](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/psychoacoustics/sound-quality/): Sharpness in acum (DIN 45692) and the ECMA-418-2 Sottek Hearing Model tonality (tu_HMS), roughness (asper) and fluctuation strength (vacil_HMS).
- [Prominent Discrete Tones (ECMA-418-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/psychoacoustics/tone-prominence/): ECMA-418-1 tone-to-noise and prominence ratios: FFT verdicts for discrete tones, ECMA-74 positions and how to choose among four tonality metrics.
- [Objective audibility of tones in noise (ISO/PAS 20065)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/psychoacoustics/tone-audibility/): ISO/PAS 20065:2016 audibility ΔL of a tone above its masking threshold: critical band, masking, peak detection and the ISO 1996-2 adjustment.
- [Psychoacoustic annoyance and fluctuation strength (Fastl & Zwicker)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/psychoacoustics/psychoacoustic-annoyance/): Fastl & Zwicker psychoacoustic annoyance (loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength), its AM-noise closed form and the Osses 2016 model.

### Speech

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/speech/): Three speech intelligibility measures: IEC 60268-16 STI rates a channel, ANSI S3.5 SII a listening condition, and STOI/ESTOI a processor. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-perception-speech.txt)
- [Speech Transmission Index (IEC 60268-16)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/speech/speech-transmission/): IEC 60268-16 speech transmission index (STI): modulation transfer function, the indirect method from an impulse response and direct STIPA.
- [Speech Intelligibility Index (SII)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/speech/speech-intelligibility/): ANSI S3.5-1997 Speech Intelligibility Index (SII) in its four band procedures: band importance, audibility, noise and hearing loss.
- [Objective intelligibility (STOI & ESTOI)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/speech/objective-intelligibility/): Correlation-based objective intelligibility of time-frequency weighted noisy speech: STOI (Taal et al. 2011) and ESTOI (Jensen & Taal 2016).

### Hearing and exposure

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/hearing/): Hearing and noise damage: ISO 7029 and ISO 389-7 thresholds, ISO 8253 audiometry, ISO 1999 hearing loss, ISO 9612 exposure and ISO 4869 protectors. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-perception-hearing.txt)
- [Hearing threshold (age and reference zero)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/hearing/hearing-threshold/): Hearing threshold by age and sex (ISO 7029:2017 median, spread and fractiles) and the ISO 389-7:2005 free- and diffuse-field reference zero.
- [Audiometric Test Methods (ISO 8253-1 and -2)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/hearing/audiometry/): Audiometric rooms and thresholds: room noise and sound field (ISO 8253-1, -2), four test methods for the hearing threshold level, and its uncertainty.
- [Occupational Noise Exposure (ISO 9612)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/hearing/occupational-exposure/): ISO 9612 task-based, job-based and full-day strategies for LEX,8h, with the Annex C uncertainty budget and the one-sided 95 % upper limit.
- [Noise-induced hearing loss (ISO 1999)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/hearing/noise-induced-hearing-loss/): ISO 1999:2013 noise-induced permanent threshold shift (NIPTS) by level, duration and frequency, combined with ISO 7029 age into HTLAN, 500 to 6000 Hz.
- [Hearing Protectors (ISO 4869-1, -2, -3 and -6)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/perception/hearing/hearing-protectors/): ISO 4869 hearing protectors: attenuation on sixteen subjects (-1), effective A-weighted level (-2), insertion loss (-3) and active earmuffs (-6).

## Rooms and buildings

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/): Room acoustics measured and predicted (ISO 3382, EN 12354-6), and sound insulation measured in the field and the laboratory and predicted by EN 12354.

### Room acoustics

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/): Room acoustics: ISO 18233 impulse responses, ISO 3382 parameters, open-plan offices, image sources, ANSI S12.2 noise and EN 12354-6 reverberation. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-buildings-rooms.txt)
- [Measuring the Room Impulse Response](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/room-impulse-response/): Room impulse response measurement with the ISO 18233 excitations: the exponential sine sweep, MLS, and source and microphone placement.
- [Room Acoustics](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/room-acoustics/): Decay analysis of a room impulse response by ISO 3382-1/2: Schroeder curve, EDT, T20, T30, clarity, definition, centre time and the fiche.
- [Open-Plan Office Acoustics (ISO 3382-3)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/open-plan-acoustics/): Open-plan office speech privacy (ISO 3382-3): D2,S, level at 4 m, distraction and privacy distances, the fiche and Long's occupant-noise prediction.
- [Image sources and the steady-state room field (Kuttruff / Vorländer / Bies)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/room-image-sources/): Image-source impulse response of a rectangular room, steady-state level, room constant, critical distance, Schroeder frequency and the room modes.
- [Spatial sound decay in workrooms (ISO 14257, ISO 11690-3)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/workroom-sound-decay/): Spatial sound decay in workrooms: the ISO 14257 curve, its descriptors DL2 and DLf, the Annex B correction and ISO 11690-3 prediction.
- [Room-noise criteria (NC / RC Mark II)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/room-noise/): Room-noise ratings (ANSI/ASA S12.2-2019): NC curves with the tangency fallback, and RC Mark II with its rumble, hiss or neutral tag.
- [Reverberation-time prediction (Sabine · Eyring · Fitzroy · Arau-Puchades)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/reverberation-prediction/): Reverberation-time prediction from volume, areas and absorption: Sabine, Eyring, Millington-Sette, Fitzroy and Arau-Puchades, with air absorption.
- [Sound absorption in enclosed spaces (EN 12354-6)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/enclosed-space-absorption/): EN 12354-6:2003 prediction of a room's absorption area and reverberation time from its surfaces, objects and air (the Clause 4 model).

### Auditorium measures of the ISO 3382-1 annexes

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/): Room acoustics: ISO 18233 impulse responses, ISO 3382 parameters, open-plan offices, image sources, ANSI S12.2 noise and EN 12354-6 reverberation. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-buildings-rooms-auditorium.txt)
- [Sound strength G (ISO 3382-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/sound-strength/): Sound strength G (ISO 3382-1): impulse-response energy against the same source at 10 m in free field, and three routes without a 10 m anechoic room.
- [Spatial impression (ISO 3382-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/spatial-impression/): Spatial impression (ISO 3382-1) with a second microphone: early lateral energy fraction, late lateral level and interaural cross correlation.
- [Stage support and uncertainty (ISO 3382-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/stage-and-uncertainty/): Stage support and uncertainty (ISO 3382-1): two measures with the source a metre away, and what a random excitation costs a reverberation time.
- [Reporting and source qualification (ISO 3382-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/rooms/reporting-and-qualification/): Printed tables of ISO 3382-1: source directivity, how many microphone positions a hall needs, the bands of each single number, and the report.

### Laboratory insulation measurement

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/): Airborne and impact insulation measured and rated: laboratory (ISO 10140, 15186, 10848), field (ISO 16283, 10052, 16032), ISO 717 ratings and façades. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-buildings-insulation-laboratory.txt)
- [Laboratory Insulation Measurement](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/insulation-lab/): Building elements in the laboratory (ISO 10140): sound reduction index R and impact level Ln without flanking, background correction and fiches.
- [Linings, Floor Coverings, Joints and Rain (ISO 10140-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/lab-application-rules/): Four application rules of ISO 10140-1:2021 (Annexes G, H, J and K): wall linings, floor coverings, sealed joints and artificial rain.
- [Sound Insulation by Intensity (ISO 15186)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/insulation-intensity/): Sound insulation by intensity (ISO 15186): RI from scanning the radiating face, Kc adaptation to ISO 10140, small-element level difference and fiches.
- [Laboratory Flanking Transmission (ISO 10848)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/flanking-lab/): Flanking transmission measured in the laboratory by ISO 10848: Kij, Dn,f, Ln,f, the Part 4 modal-overlap checks and the ceiling plenum path with Dn,c.

### Sound insulation

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/): Airborne and impact insulation measured and rated: laboratory (ISO 10140, 15186, 10848), field (ISO 16283, 10052, 16032), ISO 717 ratings and façades. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-buildings-insulation.txt)
- [Field Insulation Measurement (ISO 16283)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/insulation-field/): Field sound insulation by ISO 16283-1/-2: airborne D, DnT and R', impact L'nT and L'n, the Clause 14 test report and the ISO 12999-1 uncertainty.
- [Small Rooms: the ISO 16283 Low-Frequency Procedure](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/low-frequency-procedure/): Corner procedure that ISO 16283 requires below 25 m³: corner level, combination and 63 Hz reverberation time, for airborne, impact and façade.
- [Heavy and Soft Impact Sources (ISO 16283-2)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/heavy-impact-sources/): Rubber ball and bang machine: force exposure level, the ISO 16283-2 and JIS A 1418-2 checks, Fast maximum level and the ISO 717-2 Annex D rating.
- [Sound Insulation Survey Method (ISO 10052)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/insulation-survey/): ISO 10052 survey method: octave bands, a hand-held meter and the reverberation index, for airborne, impact, façade and service-equipment quantities.
- [Service-Equipment and Activity Noise (ISO 16032)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/service-equipment-noise/): Service-equipment noise by the ISO/DIS 16032:2023 draft: corner and reverberant positions, background correction, standardization, A and C single numbers.

### Insulation ratings and the envelope

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/): Airborne and impact insulation measured and rated: laboratory (ISO 10140, 15186, 10848), field (ISO 16283, 10052, 16032), ISO 717 ratings and façades. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-buildings-insulation-ratings.txt)
- [Insulation Ratings (ISO 717)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/insulation-ratings/): ISO 717-1 airborne and ISO 717-2 impact single-number ratings with C, Ctr and CI terms, the enlarged-range and one-decimal variants, and the ISO 717 fiche.
- [Façade Sound Insulation](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/facade-insulation/): Façade insulation measured by ISO 16283-3 (loudspeaker and road-traffic methods) and predicted by EN 12354-3, with EN 12354-4 outdoor radiation.
- [Spanish Building Code (CTE DB-HR)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/insulation/spanish-building-code/): CTE DB-HR global index: the Annex A formula over eighteen one-third-octave bands, normalized spectra, rounding, requirements and window correction.

### Insulation design

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/design/): Sound insulation before it is built: EN/ISO 12354 flanking, panels, resilient layers, and service-equipment sound from EN 15657 to EN 12354-5. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-buildings-design.txt)
- [Predicting Sound Insulation (EN 12354)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/design/insulation-prediction/): EN 12354 prediction of in-situ insulation between rooms from element data: airborne and impact flanking, vibration reduction indices and fiches.
- [Detailed Per-Band Prediction (ISO 12354)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/design/detailed-prediction/): ISO 12354-1/-2:2017 detailed model: in-situ element and junction data, flanking band by band, and the per-path contributions to R'w and L'n,w.
- [Predicting Panel Sound Insulation (mass law, coincidence, double walls)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/design/panel-sound-insulation/): Airborne insulation of panels from their properties: mass law, coincidence, orthotropic sheets, double walls, wall ties, slits, radiation and mobility.
- [Floor-Covering Impact Improvement (ISO 16251-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/design/impact-improvement/): Floor-covering impact improvement on the ISO 16251-1 mock-up: acceleration levels, ISO 717-2 weighted improvement, fiche and ISO 12354-2 estimate.
- [Predicting Resilient-Layer Performance](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/design/resilient-layers/): Resilient-layer prediction: the tapping machine, soft coverings, the 30 lg and 40 lg floating-floor laws and ISO 12354-1 Annex D wall linings.
- [Structure-borne sound power of building equipment (EN 15657)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/design/structure-borne-power/): UNE-EN 15657:2018 reception-plate method: injected power L_Ws, blocked force, characteristic power, and the free velocity and mobility of the source.
- [Installed structure-borne sound from equipment (EN 12354-5)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/buildings/design/installed-structure-borne/): Receiving-room level from structure-borne service-equipment sound (EN 12354-5:2009): coupling term D_C, installed power, per-path and total level.

## Materials and surfaces

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/): Materials and surfaces: ISO 354 absorption, ISO 9053 airflow resistance, ISO 10534 tube, absorber models, ISO 17497 diffusers and resilient layers.
- [Reading a material datasheet](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/reading-a-datasheet/): Numbers on a data sheet, a declaration of performance or a test report: what they are and how to write them into a catalogue of your own.

### Absorbers

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/absorbers/): Absorber characterisation and prediction: ISO 11654 rating, ISO 9053 airflow resistance, ISO 10534 / ASTM E2611 tube, porous and metamaterial models. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-materials-absorbers.txt)
- [Sound Absorption Measurement and Rating](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/absorbers/absorption-measurement/): Sound absorption in a reverberation room (ISO 354), its rating as alpha_w with a class (ISO 11654) and the uncertainty of both (ISO 12999-2).
- [Suspended ceilings: the EN 16487 test code](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/absorbers/suspended-ceilings/): EN 16487 for suspended ceilings: what it fixes so two laboratories agree, type E mounting 200 mm deep, the air-absorption correction and reproducibility.
- [Airflow Resistance](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/absorbers/airflow-resistance/): Airflow resistance, specific airflow resistance and resistivity of porous materials by the static (ISO 9053-1) and alternating (ISO 9053-2) methods.
- [Impedance Tube](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/absorbers/impedance-tube/): Normal-incidence absorption and impedance in the tube: ISO 10534-1 standing wave, ISO 10534-2 two microphones and ASTM E2611 transmission loss.
- [Porous and Multilayer Absorbers](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/absorbers/porous-absorbers/): Absorption prediction from material parameters: Delany-Bazley, Miki, Johnson-Champoux-Allard, transfer-matrix multilayers and the Biot layer.
- [Metamaterial Absorbers](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/absorbers/metamaterial-absorbers/): Perfect absorption with deep-subwavelength panels: critical coupling and the slow-sound slit panel with Helmholtz resonators.

### Diffusers and surfaces

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/diffusers/): Surfaces graded and designed by what they reflect: ISO 17497 scattering and diffusion, Schroeder diffusers, metadiffusers and ISO 13472 road surfaces. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-materials-diffusers.txt)
- [Diffusers and Their Coefficients](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/diffusers/diffusers/): Diffuser measurement and design: scattering (ISO 17497-1) and diffusion (ISO 17497-2), Schroeder quadratic-residue design and coefficient tables.
- [Metadiffusers](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/diffusers/metadiffusers/): Metadiffusers: with Helmholtz resonators in the slits, a 2 cm panel scatters like a 27 cm Schroeder diffuser, evaluated with ISO 17497-2.

### Surfaces measured in place

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/surfaces/): Surfaces without a sample: why a pavement is characterised where it lies, ISO 13472-1 subtraction against the ISO 13472-2 spot tube, scope and editions. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-materials-surfaces.txt)
- [In-situ Road-Surface Absorption](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/surfaces/road-absorption/): Road-surface absorption measured in situ: ISO 13472-1 subtraction with the Adrienne window, the ISO 13472-2 spot tube, and how to choose between them.

### Resilient layers

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/resilient/): Dynamic stiffness of a resilient layer, what a floating floor is designed around: its EN 29052-1 measurement and the natural frequency under a screed. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-materials-resilient.txt)
- [Dynamic stiffness of resilient materials (EN 29052-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/materials/resilient/dynamic-stiffness/): Dynamic stiffness per unit area of resilient layers under floating floors by EN 29052-1:1992, and the floor's natural frequency.

## Vibration and structure-borne sound

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/): Vibration in buildings, people and machines: ISO 7626 FRFs, ISO 10846 isolators, ISO 2631 and ISO 5349 metrics, and fault frequencies.

### Structure-borne sources

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/structural/): Chain from machine vibration to noise in other rooms: ISO 7626 FRFs, ISO 10846 isolators, ISO/TS 7849 radiated power, EN 15657, EN 12354-5 and DIN 4150-3. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-vibration-structural.txt)
- [Mechanical mobility and the FRF family (ISO 7626-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/structural/mechanical-mobility/): ISO 7626-1:2011 FRF family: receptance, mobility, accelerance and their reciprocals, conversion, the SDOF resonator and ISO 7626-2 acceptance.
- [Mobility by impact excitation (ISO 7626-5)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/structural/impact-mobility/): Mobility measured with an impact hammer by ISO 7626-5:2019: force and exponential windows, averaged H1 and coherence, and the Annex A damping correction.
- [Bending-wave transmission at plate junctions (Cremer / Craik / Hopkins)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/structural/junction-transmission/): Two routes to the coupling loss factor: bending waves and Kij at rigid X, T, L and in-line plate junctions, and experimental SEA.
- [Dynamic transfer stiffness of resilient elements (ISO 10846)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/structural/transfer-stiffness/): ISO 10846 dynamic transfer stiffness of resilient elements: its level and loss factor, and the direct, indirect and driving-point methods (Parts 2 to 5).
- [Vibration damage to structures (DIN 4150-3)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/structural/structural-damage/): DIN 4150-3 guideline values: peak particle velocity by building class and frequency, buried pipes, long-term values and the bending stress.
- [Predicting a building's own frequency (ISO 4866)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/structural/building-response/): Empirical predictors of ISO 4866 Annex D: the storey rule, three code forms for the period, the f = 46/h fit to 163 buildings and damping.

### Human vibration

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/human/): Vibration transmitted to people: ISO 8041-1 weightings, ISO 2631-1 whole-body metrics, ISO 5349 hand-arm exposure and ISO 2631-5 repeated shocks. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-vibration-human.txt)
- [Human Vibration: Whole-Body and Hand-Arm Exposure](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/human/human-vibration/): Whole-body and hand-arm vibration: ISO 8041-1 weightings, ISO 2631-1 r.m.s. and doses (VDV, MTVV, MSDV), A(8), ISO 5349 and Directive 2002/44/EC.
- [Multiple-shock whole-body vibration (ISO 2631-5)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/human/multiple-shock-vibration/): Multiple shocks by ISO 2631-5:2018: the spinal model, seat-to-spine transfer, acceleration dose, compressive stress, R and lumbar-injury risk.
- [What a seat does to the vibration (ISO 10326-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/human/seat-vibration/): ISO 10326-1 laboratory seat test: SEAT factor, three runs within 5 %, input correction and transmissibility at resonance.
- [Verifying a human-vibration meter (ISO 8041-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/human/meter-verification/): Human-vibration meter verification by ISO 8041-1: tolerances with the laboratory's uncertainty, phase, decay times and bursts.

### Machinery

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/machinery/): Machine diagnosis from vibration: bearing, gear, motor and blade-passing families from the geometry, and the band-pass and envelope route to a defect. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-vibration-machinery.txt)
- [Machine fault frequencies (Norton & Karczub)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/machinery/machine-diagnostics/): Fault frequencies of rotating machinery (Norton & Karczub, Section 8.4): bearing, gear-mesh, induction-motor and blade-pass families on an envelope.
- [Evaluating machine vibration (ISO 20816-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/machinery/machine-vibration-evaluation/): Machine grading from one broad-band measurement: ISO 20816-1 zones and change criterion, and ISO 10816-3 boundaries, ALARM and TRIP above 15 kW.

### Vibration immission

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/immission/): German immission chain: the DIN 45669-1 meter, the DIN 45672 reduction of a train passage and the DIN 4150-2 assessment for people in buildings. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-vibration-immission.txt)
- [Measuring vibration immission (DIN 45669-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/immission/vibration-meter/): DIN 45669-1 meter behind DIN 4150-2 and -3: KB weighting, KB_F severity, tolerances, the Annex E velocity and DIN 45669-2 planning.
- [Vibration next to a railway (DIN 45672)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/immission/railway-vibration/): Train passage reduced by DIN 45672-2: running r.m.s., hourly event value, one-third-octave and narrow-band spectra, and DIN 45672-1 ground constants.
- [Vibration and people in buildings (DIN 4150-2)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/immission/people-in-buildings/): DIN 4150-2 for people in buildings: Table 1 guide values by area and time of day, the assessment severity and the rules for blasting, traffic and sites.
- [Railway vibration by category of train (E DIN 4150-2)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/immission/railway-categories/): Draft E DIN 4150-2 (August 2023) for railways: one interval per passage, KB_Fmax per category, weighting per train, new and altered lines.
- [Predicting railway vibration (E DIN 45672-3)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/immission/railway-prediction/): Railway vibration in a building predicted by E DIN 45672-3: from emission to floor, the Annex A tables and the DIN 4150-2 KB values.
- [Predicting vibration before measuring (DIN 4150-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/vibration/immission/vibration-prediction/): Vibration prediction by DIN 4150-1: decay with distance, foundations and floors, blasts, falling masses, machine halls and tracks.

## Environment and transport

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/): Sound outdoors and its sources: ISO 9613 propagation, ISO 1996 rating, soundscape, CNOSSOS-EU traffic, wind turbines, noise barriers and trains.

### Assessment and regulation

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/assessment/): Environmental noise rating: ISO 1996 rating level, impulsive sound, blast statistics, a national application and ISO/TS 12913 soundscape. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-environment-assessment.txt)
- [Environmental Levels (ISO 1996-1/-2)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/assessment/environmental-levels/): Lden, Ldn and the composite rating levels of ISO 1996-1, with the ISO 1996-2 tonal adjustment, residual-noise correction and measurement uncertainty budget.
- [Impulsive-sound prominence (NT ACOU 112)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/assessment/impulsive-sound/): NT ACOU 112:2002 Nordtest method: the predicted prominence P of each impulsive sound, the graduated adjustment KI added to LAeq, and the rating level.
- [Spanish Noise Regulation (RD 1367/2007)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/assessment/spanish-noise-regulation/): Corrected level LKeq of Real Decreto 1367/2007: Kt, Kf and Ki, evaluation periods, quality objectives, immission limits and compliance.

### Outdoor sound

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/propagation/): Sound in open air: ISO 9613 propagation, ground effect, barriers, refraction, EN 1793-5 barrier reflection and ISO 17534-1 software checks. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-environment-propagation.txt)
- [Outdoor Sound Propagation](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/propagation/outdoor-propagation/): Outdoor sound propagation from a point source by ISO 9613-1 and -2: divergence, air absorption, ground, barriers and meteorology, per term and octave band.
- [Spherical ground effect and advanced barriers (Attenborough / Salomons / Bies)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/propagation/ground-barriers/): Weyl-Van der Pol spherical-wave reflection over finite-impedance ground and wave-theory diffraction: Kurze-Anderson, rigid half-plane, thick barriers.
- [Atmospheric refraction: ray tracing and the parabolic equation (Salomons / Attenborough)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/propagation/atmospheric-refraction/): Ray tracing and the Green's Function parabolic equation (GFPE) in a refracting atmosphere: sound-speed profiles, curved rays and shadow zones.
- [Sound reflection of a noise barrier in situ (EN 1793-5)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/propagation/barrier-reflection/): EN 1793-5 sound reflection index of a road noise barrier measured in situ: signal subtraction, Adrienne window, DL_RI and the low frequency limit.
- [Quality of outdoor sound software (ISO 17534-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/propagation/software-quality/): Outdoor sound software checked by ISO 17534-1:2015: certified test cases, quantiles of a faster configuration and precision across programs.

### Environmental sources

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/sources/): Source descriptors for prediction: CNOSSOS-EU road and rail emission, ISO 11819-1 road surfaces, ISO 3095 rail vehicles and IEC 61400-11 wind turbines. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-environment-sources.txt)
- [CNOSSOS-EU road traffic source emission](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/sources/cnossos-road-emission/): CNOSSOS-EU road traffic emission (Directive 2002/49/EC Annex II): rolling and propulsion power per vehicle category, corrections and power per metre.
- [CNOSSOS-EU railway source emission](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/sources/cnossos-rail-emission/): CNOSSOS-EU railway emission (Directive 2002/49/EC Annex II): roughness, contact filter, impact, squeal, traction, aerodynamic noise and bridges.
- [Railway rolling-stock noise: the ISO 3095 type test](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/sources/rolling-stock-noise/): Train, locomotive and wagon noise by the ISO 3095:2013 type test: stationary, constant-speed, starting and braking tests on an EN 15610/EN 15461 track.
- [Road-surface noise: the statistical pass-by method (ISO 11819-1)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/sources/road-surface-pass-by/): Road-surface noise by the ISO 11819-1 statistical pass-by method: how much a surface adds, level against log speed, the SPBI and the Annex E example.
- [Wind-turbine noise: apparent sound power and tonal audibility (IEC 61400-11)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/sources/wind-turbine-noise/): IEC 61400-11 wind-turbine emission: apparent sound power level at the rotor centre, and the tonal-audibility chain that decides if a tone is audible.
- [Wind turbine sound at a dwelling (IEC TS 61400-11-2)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/environment/sources/wind-turbine-receptor/): Wind turbine sound at a dwelling by IEC TS 61400-11-2:2024: wind shear, indoor low frequency, emergence, amplitude modulation and rating level.

## Aircraft noise

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/aircraft/): Aircraft noise with international metrics: ICAO Annex 16 EPNL, ECAC Doc 29 airport contours, ECAC Doc 32 rotorcraft and the EASA ANP database.

- [Airport noise (ECAC Doc 29)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/aircraft/airport-noise/): Airport noise by ECAC Doc 29: the noise-power-distance engine, per-segment corrections of a single event and SEL contours on a ground grid.
- [Rotorcraft noise: the hemisphere method (ECAC Doc 32 / NORAH2)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/aircraft/rotorcraft-noise/): Rotorcraft noise by the ECAC Doc 32 / NORAH2 hemisphere method: source, propagation, flight-condition interpolation, SEL, LASmax and EPNL contours.
- [The ANP fleet database](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/aircraft/anp-fleet/): ECAC Doc 29 chain for a real aircraft: the EASA ANP database of NPD curves and default trajectories, fixed-point profiles, event levels and contours.
- [NPD data for the air at the airport](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/aircraft/npd-atmosphere/): ANP NPD curves recalculated for a study's temperature, humidity and pressure by ECAC Doc 29 Vol. 2 Appendix D, with SAE ARP 5534 or 866A absorption.

## Underwater acoustics

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/underwater/): Sound in the sea: ISO 18405 levels, ISO 17208 ship noise, ISO 18406 pile driving, propagation up to numerical solvers, and marine-mammal criteria.
- [Underwater acoustics: radiated noise and pile driving (ISO 18405 / 17208 / 18406)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/underwater/underwater-acoustics/): ISO 18405 levels re 1 µPa, ship radiated noise and monopole source level by Lloyd's mirror (ISO 17208), and pile-driving exposure (ISO 18406).
- [Underwater sound propagation: propagation loss, sound speed, sonar, seabed and ambient noise](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/underwater/underwater-propagation/): Closed-form underwater propagation: spreading, absorption, Weston's four regimes, sound speed, the sonar equation and ambient noise.
- [Underwater propagation solvers: modes, rays, beams and the parabolic equation](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/underwater/underwater-solvers/): Underwater fields beyond closed forms: normal modes, ray and Gaussian beam tracing, eigenrays, sloping bottoms and the split-step parabolic equation.
- [Marine-mammal noise exposure: audiograms, auditory weighting and injury criteria](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/underwater/marine-mammal-exposure/): Marine mammals: Southall et al. (2019) audiograms, NMFS 2024, NMFS 2018 or Southall weightings, TTS and injury criteria, pile-driving exposure.

## Sources and devices

### Sound power and intensity

- [Sound Power in a Duct (ISO 5136)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/sound-power-in-duct/): Fan sound power by the ISO 5136 in-duct method: averaged level, the C1, C2 and C3,4 corrections, the A-weighted total and reproducibility.
- [Sound Power of Multisource Industrial Plants (ISO 8297)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/sound-power-plant/): Sound power of petrochemical complexes, quarries or crushing plants by ISO 8297: contour, microphone positions, corrections and uncertainty.

### Sound power on an enveloping surface

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/): Sound power by pressure, reverberation room, duct, intensity or vibration (ISO 3740 family, ISO 9614), its ISO 4871 declaration, and IEC 61043 intensity. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-devices-emission-enveloping.txt)
- [Sound Power by Pressure Methods (ISO 3744 / ISO 3746 / ISO 3745)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/sound-power-pressure/): Sound power from sound pressure: ISO 3744 and ISO 3746 enveloping surfaces with K1 and K2, the ISO 3745 precision method, and a burst's energy level.
- [Free Field and Reference Sources (ISO 26101 / ISO 6926)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/free-field-qualification/): Qualification of an anechoic or hemi-anechoic room (ISO 26101 against ISO 3745 Annex A), and calibration and verdict of a reference source (ISO 6926).
- [Sound Power of Steam Turbine Sets (IEC 61063)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/sound-power-turbines/): Airborne noise of steam turbine sets by the IEC 61063 test code: measurement surface, key microphone positions, background and environmental corrections.

### Sound power in a reverberant field

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/): Sound power by pressure, reverberation room, duct, intensity or vibration (ISO 3740 family, ISO 9614), its ISO 4871 declaration, and IEC 61043 intensity. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-devices-emission-reverberant.txt)
- [Sound Power in the Reverberation Room (ISO 3741)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/sound-power-reverberation/): Sound power in a qualified reverberation room by ISO 3741: the direct method with corrections, the comparison method, and a burst's energy level.
- [Sound Power in Small Test Rooms (ISO 3743)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/sound-power-test-rooms/): Sound power of small sources in a hard-walled room (ISO 3743-1) or a special reverberation room (ISO 3743-2), with room qualification.
- [Sound Power in Situ by Comparison (ISO 3747)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/sound-power-in-situ/): Sound power of a machine where it works, by comparison with a reference source (ISO 3747): background correction, grade and uncertainty.
- [Sound Power in the 16 kHz Octave (ISO 9295)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/sound-power-high-frequency/): Sound power in the 16 kHz octave by ISO 9295: room constant, direct level, comparison with a reference source, and 43 misprinted table cells.

### Sound intensity and sound power from it

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/): Sound power by pressure, reverberation room, duct, intensity or vibration (ISO 3740 family, ISO 9614), its ISO 4871 declaration, and IEC 61043 intensity. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-devices-emission-intensity.txt)
- [Sound Power by Intensity Scanning (ISO 9614-2 / ISO 9614-3)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/sound-power-intensity/): Sound power from scanned intensity: the ISO 9614-2 engineering and survey methods with field indicators and achieved grade, and ISO 9614-3 precision.
- [Sound Intensity (p-p method)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/emission/intensity/): Two-microphone sound intensity per IEC 61043 with the ISO 9614-1 field indicators.

### Electroacoustics

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/electroacoustics/): Devices that make sound: IEC 60268 distortion, loudspeakers, microphones and headphones, IEC 60118-4 hearing loops, swept-sine THD and BS.1770 loudness. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-devices-electroacoustics.txt)
- [Electroacoustics: distortion and frequency response (IEC 60268-3 / Bendat & Piersol)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/electroacoustics/electroacoustics/): IEC 60268-3 distortion: THD, THD+N and SINAD in the AES17 bandwidth, intermodulation, DIM, weighted THD, dynamic range, H1/H2 responses and coherence.
- [Loudspeaker Characterisation (IEC 60268-5)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/electroacoustics/loudspeakers/): Loudspeaker characterisation by IEC 60268-5: sensitivity at 1 W / 1 m, the baffled piston, the data sheet and gain before feedback.
- [Microphone Characterisation (IEC 60268-4)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/electroacoustics/microphones/): Microphone characterisation by IEC 60268-4: sensitivity in mV/Pa, directional patterns, inherent noise in dB(A) and dB(468), and the data sheet.
- [Swept-sine distortion and phase utilities (Farina / Novak)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/electroacoustics/swept-sine-distortion/): Harmonic-distortion separation from one exponential sweep (Farina, Novak): THD against frequency, minimum phase, group delay and excess phase.
- [Audio-Frequency Induction Loops (IEC 60118-4)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/electroacoustics/induction-loops/): Hearing loops by IEC 60118-4 and IEC 62489-1: the 400 mA/m reference, loop field, test signals and meter, verdicts and the overload test.
- [Headphones and Earphones (IEC 60268-7)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/electroacoustics/headphones/): Headphones by IEC 60268-7 with the IEC 60268-1 programme signal: impedance, characteristic voltages, coupler and ear responses, and crosstalk.

### Broadcast

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/broadcast/): Two broadcast meters: ITU-R BS.1770 gated loudness in LUFS with the EBU R 128 target and true peak, and the ITU-R BS.468-4 quasi-peak meter. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-devices-broadcast.txt)
- [Programme loudness and true peak (ITU-R BS.1770 / EBU R 128)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/broadcast/program-loudness/): Programme loudness by ITU-R BS.1770-5 and EBU R 128: gated LUFS, momentary and short-term meters, loudness range and true peak.
- [Quasi-peak programme meter (ITU-R BS.468-4)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/broadcast/quasi-peak/): ITU-R BS.468-4 quasi-peak detector: tone-burst acceptance windows instead of a time constant, and the 0.775 V calibration behind dBqps.

### Noise control

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/): Industrial noise control on the path: fan-to-room duct calculation, room-to-room chain, reactive silencers and machine enclosures. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-devices-noise-control.txt)
- [Duct-borne noise: fan to room](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/duct-path/): HVAC duct noise from fan to room: fan power, attenuation, regenerated noise, room effect and NC verdict, checked on Long's Table 14.9.
- [Room to room: partition, receiving room, criterion](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/room-to-room/): Room-to-room noise reduction: source-room level, partition transmission loss, receiving-room absorption and NC verdict (Norton & Karczub).
- [Silencers](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/silencers/): Reactive silencers by four-pole matrices (expansion chamber, Helmholtz, quarter-wave and extended-tube resonators) compared with dissipative ones.
- [Industrial noise control: HVAC and enclosures](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/noise-control/): HVAC duct attenuation and flow noise (end reflection, elbows, plenums) and machine-enclosure insertion loss, from Bies, Hansen & Howard.
- [HVAC noise the German way (VDI 2081)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/vdi2081-air-systems/): VDI 2081 from a fan's duty point to the room level: duct attenuation and flow noise, splitter silencer and room, with the Part 2 worked example.

### Measuring a device that is already built

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/): Industrial noise control on the path: fan-to-room duct calculation, room-to-room chain, reactive silencers and machine enclosures. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-devices-noise-control-measured.txt)
- [Measuring a silencer (ISO 7235 and ISO 11691)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/silencer-measurement/): Catalogue insertion loss of a silencer: the ISO 7235 substitution measurement, its survey sibling ISO 11691, the octave fold and repeatability.
- [Enclosures and cabins measured (ISO 11546, ISO 11957)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/enclosure-cabin-insulation/): Machine enclosures (ISO 11546) and operator cabins (ISO 11957) measured: two determinations, substitute sources, the room check and acceptance.
- [Silencers, screens and barriers in situ (ISO 11820, ISO 11821, ISO 10847)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/in-situ-noise-control/): Silencers (ISO 11820), removable screens (ISO 11821) and barriers (ISO 10847) measured in situ, and why their background corrections are never merged.

### Control valve noise (IEC 60534-8)

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/): Industrial noise control on the path: fan-to-room duct calculation, room-to-room chain, reactive silencers and machine enclosures. · [full text](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-devices-noise-control-valves.txt)
- [Control valve noise (IEC 60534-8-3)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/control-valve-noise/): Control valve noise by IEC 60534-8-3: five flow regimes, the peak frequency, the pipe transmission loss and the level 1 m outside.
- [Hydrodynamic valve noise (IEC 60534-8-4)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/devices/noise-control/valve-cavitation/): Noise of a control valve in a liquid line by IEC 60534-8-4: whether it cavitates, two acoustical efficiencies, two peak frequencies and the level at 1 m.

## Wave simulation

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/simulation/): Sound field computed by a deterministic 2D FDTD solver and its elastic P-SV companion, with Rayleigh and Scholte waves and fluid-solid coupling.
- [Where heavy work runs: CPU or GPU, here or on a node](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/simulation/where-it-runs/): Where phonometry's simulations and videos run: here or on a node over SSH, on a CPU or GPU, which device and encoder to ask for, and the page for each.
- [2D FDTD wave simulation](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/simulation/fdtd-simulation/): Deterministic 2D acoustic FDTD solver: sources, probes, obstacles, rigid, impedance and absorbing boundaries, following Attenborough & Van Renterghem.
- [Elastic waves and fluid-solid coupling](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/simulation/elastic-waves/): Elastic P-SV waves by FDTD: the Virieux (1986) scheme, Rayleigh and Scholte waves, and fluid-solid coupling validated against Brekhovskikh & Godin.
- [Where a simulation runs: NumPy, CuPy and torch](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/simulation/compute/): Acoustic and elastic FDTD engines on NumPy, CuPy on an NVIDIA GPU or PyTorch: Compute, use(), PHONOMETRY_COMPUTE, the NumPy fallback and provenance.
- [Sending a simulation to a remote node](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/simulation/remote-node/): Remote runs of fdtd_simulation and elastic_fdtd_simulation over SSH: the hosts file, Docker or Python nodes, the NumPy fallback and security.

## Theory and reference

The theory pages travel in their own shard (https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-theory.txt), the glossary in another (https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-glossary.txt), and the rest of the reference in https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/llms/llms-reference.txt.

- [Overview](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/): Theory, evidence and vocabulary: derivations behind the modules, the conformance report, defects found in the sources, the bibliography and the glossary.
- [API Reference](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/api/): Every public function, class and constant in phonometry, generated from the source docstrings.
- [Bibliography](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/bibliography/): Every source the guides cite, by area: standards with their catalogue records, books and papers with a verified DOI or publisher link, each with a note.
- [Same bits on every machine](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/determinism/): Determinism: why floating point drifts, how a designed filter stays byte-identical on any CPU, BLAS or thread count, what still differs, and the evidence.
- [Glossary](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/glossary/): Acoustic quantities the guides compute most, each with symbol, one-sentence definition, unit, defining standard and clause, and the guide computing it.
- [Theoretical Background](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/theory/): Derivations by domain: six pages tracing each shared method to its clause, equation and table, and the areas whose theory stays in its guide.
- [Theory: Environment and Transport](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/theory/environment-transport/): Environmental descriptors, impulsive-sound adjustments, outdoor propagation, occupational exposure and sound power determination behind phonometry.
- [Theory: Materials and Surfaces](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/theory/materials-surfaces/): Surface scattering and diffusion, in-situ road-surface absorption and acoustic material characterisation behind phonometry.
- [Theory: Perception and Hearing](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/theory/perception/): Equal-loudness contours, loudness models, sound-quality metrics, tone prominence, speech intelligibility and hearing statistics behind phonometry.
- [Theory: Rooms and Buildings](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/theory/rooms-buildings/): Room acoustics, noise criteria, sound insulation and flanking prediction behind phonometry.
- [Theory: Signal Analysis](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/theory/signal-analysis/): Filter bank design, frequency weightings, time integration, level and exposure metrics, sound intensity and the GUM uncertainty framework behind phonometry.
- [Theory: Vibration](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/theory/vibration/): Human vibration weightings and metrics, the multiple-shock spinal model, and the point mobility and radiation efficiency of structure-borne sound.

## Evidence and provenance

- [Conformance report](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/conformance/): every check, with the standard, the clause, the normative expected value, the value the library computes and the delta
- [Errata in published sources](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/errata/): defects found in published standards, each re-derived from that standard's own normative clauses
- [Published catalogues](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/): every value this library read off a printed page, with the book, the table and the page it came from, and what the page printed where a number is missing
- [Report fiches](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/reports/): every PDF fiche the library renders, in the reporting format its standard defines, with the guide that explains the measurement behind each one
- [Bibliography](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/bibliography/)
- [About the author and the method](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/about/)

- [Errata in Rossing (2014)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/errata/rossing/): 6 entries
- [Errata in Southall et al. (2019)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/errata/southall/): 1 entry
- [Errata in VDI 2081](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/errata/vdi-2081/): 6 entries
- [Errata in Ver & Beranek (2006)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/errata/ver-beranek/): 4 entries
- [Errata in Vigran (2008)](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/errata/vigran/): 3 entries

## Properties that are not errata

- [Source properties that are not errata](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/errata/not-errata/): Properties of the published sources that look like misprints and are not, recorded so that nobody corrects the library to match them.

## Published catalogues

Every material, gas and fluid the library reads from a printed page, from elastic constants to fluid states, with its source table and what its cell said. One page per catalogue, each listed here with the rows it tables (index: https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/).

- [Catalogue of absorption coefficients](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/absorption-coefficients/) (459 rows): What finishes absorbed in a reverberation room, band by band, with the mounting and the source of each row, and the absorption area of audiences and air.
- [Catalogue of air attenuation](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/air-attenuation/) (6 rows): The air attenuation coefficient, band by band, for the six temperature and humidity conditions a building standard's room model tabulates, in neper per metre.
- [Catalogue of carpets](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/carpets/) (19 rows): Nineteen carpets rated by their noise reduction coefficient, on bare concrete and on a hair pad, with the weight, height, surface and fibre of the pile.
- [Catalogue of damping materials](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/damping-materials/) (17 rows): Seventeen commercial damping materials: the peak loss factor, the temperature of the peak at 10 Hz, 100 Hz and 1 kHz, and the storage and loss moduli.
- [Catalogue of damping treatments](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/damping-treatments/) (8 rows): Eight asphalt felt treatments rated by how fast they damp a standard steel plate at 160 Hz, in decibels per second, from 1 dB/s to 400.
- [Catalogue of diffusion coefficients](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/diffusion-coefficients/) (87 rows): Diffusion coefficients of semicylinders, semiellipses, triangles and other surfaces, computed with a two-dimensional boundary element model.
- [Catalogue of duct walls](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/duct-walls/) (46 rows): Forty-six measurements of the sound that leaves a sheet metal duct through its wall and the sound that enters it, by size, shape, gauge and lining.
- [Catalogue of dynamic moduli of resilient materials](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/dynamic-modulus-of-resilient-materials/) (6 rows): The dynamic modulus of six resilient materials a floating floor is laid on, printed as ranges and measured under a static load of about 2 kPa.
- [Catalogue of fluids](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/fluids/) (25 rows): Named fluid states: liquids and gases at the temperature each page states, read from two books, and four airs fixed by the models and standards that use them.
- [Catalogue of gases](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/gases/) (43 rows): The molar mass and the ratio of specific heats of gases, which close the ideal-gas state at any temperature and pressure, as two books print them.
- [Catalogue of ground surfaces](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/ground-surfaces/) (105 rows): The effective flow resistivity the outdoor propagation models take for a ground, with the model each value was fitted with, and the ground classes A to H.
- [Catalogue of impact insulation](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/impact-insulation/) (71 rows): The impact insulation class of floor-ceiling constructions, and the improvement surface treatments and floor finishes give over a bare concrete floor.
- [Catalogue of the nonlinearity parameter B/A](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/nonlinearity-parameter-ba/) (164 rows): A hundred and sixty-four values of the nonlinearity parameter B/A of water, organic liquids, liquid metals and liquefied gases, each with its paper.
- [Catalogue of the nonlinearity parameter of solids](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/nonlinearity-parameter-of-solids/) (8 rows): The ultrasonic nonlinearity parameter of eight solids at room temperature, averaged over the three pure longitudinal directions of a cubic crystal.
- [Catalogue of orthotropic wood](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/orthotropic-wood/) (2 rows): The four elastic constants of a thin orthotropic plate for the two woods a stringed instrument is made of, with the author's own guesses marked.
- [Catalogue of plateau-method constants](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/plateau-method-constants/) (8 rows): The three numbers the plateau method sketches a single panel's transmission loss with: mass per millimetre, plateau height and plateau width.
- [Catalogue of porous materials](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/porous-materials/) (194 rows): Porosity, flow resistivity, tortuosity and the other inputs of the equivalent-fluid and poroelastic models, as measured specimens and as compiled ranges.
- [Catalogue of predicted scattering coefficients](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/predicted-scattering-coefficients/) (119 rows): Scattering coefficients computed with two- and three-dimensional boundary element models, kept apart from the measured ones, with the solver of each row.
- [Catalogue of resilient layers](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/resilient-layers/) (15 rows): Fifteen resilient layers a floating floor is laid on, each with the dynamic stiffness per unit area measured on it, its density and its thickness.
- [Catalogue of resistive facings](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/resistive-facings/) (29 rows): Twenty-nine wire meshes, glass cloths and sintered metal sheets, each with the flow resistance of unit area of it, which is not a resistivity per metre.
- [Catalogue of scattering coefficients](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/scattering-coefficients/) (46 rows): Measured scattering coefficients of surfaces, band by band, each row credited to the paper it came from: the values a room modeller starts from.
- [Catalogue of solids](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/solids/) (260 rows): Elastic constants, wave speeds and loss factors of solids, read from nine tables in eight books, each row with the table and the page it came from.
- [Catalogue of transmission loss](https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/reference/catalogues/transmission-loss/) (255 rows): What partitions did in a laboratory, band by band, and the sound transmission class of walls, doors, windows and floor-ceiling systems.

## Spanish

Every page above also exists in Spanish under the `/es/` prefix, for example https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/es/start/getting-started/. The two trees are kept at parity by a build check.

## Markdown copies

Every page listed here but the ones named at the end of this section has a Markdown copy beside it at `<page>/index.md`, for example https://docs.jmrp.io/phonometry/start/getting-started/index.md, and its Spanish twin under `/es/` has one too where the page is translated. The 269 pages of the API reference are in English only: at the Spanish address the site shows the English page, which points to its English copy. The 52 pages that show their data through a component publish none and are read on the page itself: the two landing pages, the 23 catalogues and the "Report fiches" page in both languages and the Spanish "Conformance report" and "Glossary" pages.
